mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: FEDFUNDS rising above 2.5% triggers negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as tight monetary policy raises borrowing costs.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns not negative when FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% (p > 0.05 t-test).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent rise in GDPC1 (demand) and INDPRO (supply) signals robust economic activity, driving positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Proxies not significantly correlated (p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-month window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, sustained FEDFUNDS decline signals easing, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Regime not late-cycle expansion or returns not positive over 60 days when FEDFUNDS declines.

mechanism_narrative: UNRATE falling below 3.5% indicates improving labor market, driving positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
Rising GDPC1 (demand) and INDPRO (supply) both above thresholds signal robust activity, driving positive 20-day returns.
failure_condition: Proxies not significantly correlated (p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-month window.

mechanism_narrative: Quarterly GDPC1 growth exceeding 1% signals expanding demand, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth not above 1% but returns positive (p > 0.05 t-test).

mechanism_narrative: INDPRO falling below 105 indicates weakening supply, resulting in negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
